name: Colchicine
mechanism: Inhibits neutrophil chemotaxis and phagocytosis by disrupting microtubules
dosing: Acute gout: 500mcg 2-4 times daily until relief (max 6mg per course). Prophylaxis: 500mcg OD-BD
contraindications: Severe renal/hepatic impairment, blood disorders, pregnancy
interactions: Macrolides, statins, ciclosporin (↑ toxicity), P-glycoprotein inhibitors
monitoring: FBC, U&Es, LFTs if prolonged use. Watch for toxicity signs
sideEffects: Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, bone marrow suppression (toxicity)
pharmacokinetics: Hepatic metabolism, renal excretion, narrow therapeutic index
clinicalPearls: Start at first sign of acute gout. High dose regimens no longer recommended due to toxicity. Stop if diarrhoea develops
indication: Acute gout, gout prophylaxis during urate-lowering therapy initiation, familial Mediterranean fever
